name: Qhapaq Ñan state road network
summary: The Qhapaq Ñan, the Inka state's connected network of highland and coastal roads linking Cusco to its provinces, used for messengers, armies and officials.
description: Connected highland and coastal Inka state road routes linking Cusco with provincial centres and incorporating earlier Andean routes.
tier_reason: A bounded technical contribution, transmission episode or documented configuration useful within a specific history; no broad dependence claim is established.
why: The expanding Inka state needed to move officials, messages, troops and goods across the steep, varied terrain of the Andes.

places.note: Andean regions of Tawantinsuyu (Inka empire), not limited to Peru and Chile

date.label: by the end of the 15th century
date.basis: UNESCO describes a functioning state network reaching its maximum expansion in the 15th century.

events.statement: The connected Inka road system supported state movement and communications by the fifteenth-century expansion.
